findings.title: $__range check ineffective after interpolation breaks splitting logic for range queries
findings.body: The change interpolates queries upfront via `applyTemplateVariables` (line 299), but the `querySupportsSplitting` check at line 282 is still applied to the interpolated queries via `partition` at line 300. The check `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` is intended to prevent splitting queries that contain `$__range`, but after `applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range` with a literal duration (e.g., `3d` or `259200000ms`), the check always returns true. As a result, queries like `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range])` will now be split into sub-requests, but the `$__range` literal value baked into the query is the FULL range (since interpolation uses `request.range`), not the split range. This produces semantically incorrect results: each sub-request queries `[3d]` worth of data but only returns a window of 1d. The accompanying comment at lines 285-286 explicitly states that `$__range` queries should NOT be split. The `isQueryWithRangeVariable` check needs to be applied before interpolation (e.g., on the original `request.targets`), or `$__range` needs to be left uninterpolated and re-applied per sub-request.

findings.title: No test covers $__range behavior after interpolation change
findings.body: The new test 'Interpolates queries before execution' (line 75) only verifies `$__auto` and `$step` interpolation. There is no test for `$__range` queries after this change. A regression test should verify that queries containing `$__range` are still routed to the non-splitting path (i.e., they should not be split because the interpolated `$__range` value would be incorrect for split sub-requests). Without such a test, the `$__range` regression described in the primary finding could go undetected.
